statement.p: Let f(x,y,z)=x+yz and let \mathcal{C} be the line segment from P=(0,0,0) to (4,3,5).
(a) Calculate f(\mathbf{c}(t)) and \,ds=\Vert \mathbf{c}'(t)\Vert\,dt for the parametrization \mathbf{c}(t)=(4 t,3 t,5 t) for 0\le t \le 1.

static.solution: (a) We substitute x=4 t, y=3 t, z=5 t in the function f( x,y,z )=x+yz to find f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right): f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)=4 t+( 3 t )( 5 t )=4 t+15 t^2 We differentiate the vector \mathbf{c}(t) and compute the length of the derivative vector: {\mathbf{c}}'(t)=\frac{d}{dt}\left\lt 4 t,3 t,5 t \right> = \left\lt 4,3,5 \right>\quad\Rightarrow\quad {\| \mathbf{c}}'(t) \|=\sqrt{{4}^2+ {3}^2+ {5}^2}=\sqrt{50} Hence, ds=\| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| \,dt=\sqrt{50} \,dt (b) Computing the scalar line integral, we obtain \int_{\mathcal{C}} f( x,y,z ) \,ds =\int_0^1 f\left(\mathbf{c}(t)\right)\| {\mathbf{c}}'(t)\| \,dt =\int_0^1 (4t+15t^{2})\cdot \sqrt{50} \,dt= \sqrt{50}\left(2 t^2+\frac{15}3 t^3\right)\bigg|_0^1 =\sqrt{50}\left(2+\frac{15}3\right)= \frac{21 \sqrt{50}}{3} \approx 49.4975
